sections.value: Coding agents now build software in hours, but the steps before the build still run at human speed. Ideas wait for someone to write them up, and requirements and design pass through meetings and handoffs before an engineer can plan. (Source: the AI-native SDLC playbook, stages Plan, Design and Build.)

rows.text: Brainstorm with an LLM, driven by an intent template chosen at the start
Generate intent.md with metadata (ID, author, dates, status, version)
Versioned, editable templates for every document
Stable requirement IDs traced from intent to spec, plan and tests
Each stage unlocks only when the previous one is approved
Hand off a repository scaffold any coding agent can build from
One project per folder, with its config and libraries in a .keel folder
Change requests across stages, listed and tracked on a Changes page
On demand, for any folder, an AI readiness report: a local scan against the Keel standard, then a model review of the gaps and of the AI files the user chooses to share
Discuss a change with the assistant in a chat grounded in Keel's documents; only the user's explicit agreement creates the change request, and the discussion is kept with it

sections.value: Proposers (engineers, product managers, anyone with an idea), coding agents, git hosting (GitHub first), LLM providers.

- Web UI, not a VS Code extension.
- Not tied to one model or one coding agent.
- Single user first.
- Stops at plan and scaffold: no code generation inside Keel.

- Public name: "Keel" is already used by other developer tools. Fine as a codename.
- How should a change upstream affect later documents? (Answered by CR-0003: change requests across stages.)
